issues.description: The problem specification and UML require Animal.messageOnFeed() to be abstract and return a String, but the solution implements messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (with subclasses returning FeedResponse). This changes the intended method signature and return type, introducing a structural mismatch that can confuse students about what to implement and how feed messages are produced/printed.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent with the problem statement and UML: change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String, and update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the appropriate String messages. Remove or adapt the FeedResponse class if present (or keep it but do not use it as the method return type). Update Farm.feedAllAnimals() to print the returned String messages directly.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution introduces a new FeedResponse type and implements messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. The FeedResponse class does not appear in the problem description or the template. This creates an unexpected identifier/type (FeedResponse) and a mismatched API for the same conceptual operation (feeding an animal), which will confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem and template by having messageOnFeed() return String (remove or avoid using FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement and template to document the FeedResponse type and change the specified signature to messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse. Ensure all examples, UML, and templates mention FeedResponse if option B is chosen.
